title: Escaped encrypted PEM key keeps DEK-Info line and body after "Proc-Type:" in ESCAPED_PRIVATE_KEY_PATTERN
notes: Observation: `ESCAPED_PRIVATE_KEY_PATTERN` stops at the space after `Proc-Type:` in a key escaped onto one line (`-----\\nProc-Type: 4,ENCRYPTED\\nDEK-Info: ...`), leaving the DEK-Info line and the body; Atrium fixed its copy in `94f3425` by matching the two headers first. Evidence: 0 such keys in the archive or in segment generation `02f92e0d` (rg, 2026-11-06), so the redaction of that day did not need it; adding the header alternative here fails `sonarjs/regex-complexity` (22 > 20). Next step: match headers outside the regex, as `isPrivateKeyMaterial` does, and add the Atrium test `test_an_escaped_encrypted_key_goes_with_its_headers`.

2026-11-24 audit: still open. scripts/lib/conversations/constants/ESCAPED_PRIVATE_KEY_PATTERN.ts unchanged (body class [A-Za-z0-9+/=] and \\+[rn] stops at the space after Proc-Type:); no header handling there. Atrium counterpart already has test_an_escaped_encrypted_key_goes_with_its_headers (p/atrium/tests/test_vendor_token_redaction.py:270). Prior evidence: 0 such keys in archive, so low impact. Next: strip Proc-Type/DEK-Info headers outside the regex as isPrivateKeyMaterial.ts does, add a test in CONVERSATION_REDACTION_PATTERNS_TEST.ts.
result: Escaped encrypted PEM key keeps DEK-Info line and body after "Proc-Type:" in ESCAPED_PRIVATE_KEY_PATTERN
evidence: ESCAPED_PRIVATE_KEY_PATTERN now consumes Proc-Type and DEK-Info headers; new test 'an escaped encrypted private key goes with its headers' reproduced the leak on the old pattern and passes; CONVERSATION_REDACTION_PATTERNS_TEST.ts 74 pass, type-check exit 0.
